highlights.text: He has faint laugh lines around his mouth and eyes that I’ve never seen before, and that shakes me: the passage of time, etched on his face. I used to know him better than anyone in the world, and now I don’t know him at all.

He’s right, of course; I know that intellectually. But it’s so difficult to break out of an established role—not just as business partners, but as sisters. Libby’s always been the trailblazer, the leader. Since the day I was born, I’ve watched her, how she interacts with the world, molding myself around her.

Yes, she saved me after Josh left in college, but I would’ve done the same for her in a heartbeat—she’s just never given me the opportunity. She’s always been so strong, almost annoyingly so, but maybe she felt like she had no other option. No one that she could lean on.
I don’t think she has any idea how much I idolized her as a child. How much I still do. She’ll never understand what it’s like to be the little sister, always in her shadow, watching her every move.
